issues.t: Air suspension (Airmatic) sagging or compressor failure
issues.sym: One corner or the whole car sits low after parking, the car is slow to rise, the compressor runs loudly or often, or a 'Car too low' warning appears.
issues.why: The rubber air bags in the struts crack and leak with age, and the compressor wears out from running constantly to make up for leaks. If the compressor dies, the car can become undrivable.
issues.next: Don't drive on a sagging corner, as it overworks the compressor. Have an independent Mercedes specialist find the leak; fixing a leaking strut early can save the compressor.

issues.t: Balance shaft or timing idler gear wears out
issues.sym: Check engine light with camshaft/crankshaft timing codes (P0016 or P0017), then a rattle from the timing chain. Left alone, the engine can be destroyed.
issues.why: On early 5.5L V8 engines the idler gear that drives the timing system was made of a soft metal that wears prematurely, letting the timing chain go slack. Engines built from about 2008 on got improved gears.
issues.next: If you see P0016/P0017, stop driving hard and get a specialist diagnosis right away. Check the engine serial number to see if yours has the improved gear.

issues.t: Electronic brake pump (SBC) wears out or fails
issues.sym: A brake warning on the dash, then a hard pedal that needs much more force to stop the car.
issues.why: Early CLS models used Sensotronic Brake Control, a brake-by-wire system whose pump has a limited number of brake cycles. When it reaches its limit or fails, the brakes fall back to a weak backup mode.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Ask a Mercedes dealer whether any old SBC warranty coverage or recall work applies.

issues.t: Glass sunroof panel can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The glass panel of the sliding sunroof can separate from its frame and fly off while driving.
issues.why: The bond between the glass and the sliding roof frame can deteriorate with age.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 19V-918, 21V-196, 22V-954 and 24V-874. The dealer will inspect the bonding and replace the sunroof panel free if needed.

issues.t: Head bolts corrode and leak coolant (AMG 6.2L V8)
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping while the oil level rises, milky sludge in the oil, white smoke from the exhaust and a rough idle. A large leak can lock up the engine.
issues.why: The head bolts on early 6.2L AMG engines corrode and lose clamping force, letting coolant leak into the cylinders and oil. Engines built after about mid-2010 have improved bolts.
issues.next: Stop driving if coolant is disappearing and the oil looks milky. Have a cooling-system pressure test and oil analysis done; replacing the bolts early can prevent a ruined engine.

issues.t: Ticking from worn camshafts (AMG 6.2L V8)
issues.sym: A ticking noise for a few seconds on a cold start that gradually lasts longer, later misfires and lost power.
issues.why: The camshaft lobes and the followers that ride on them wear on the 6.2L AMG engine. Severe wear can break followers.
issues.next: Have a specialist inspect the cams through the valve covers. Keep oil changes frequent with the correct oil.

issues.t: Intake manifold flaps stick or break
issues.sym: Reduced power, worse fuel economy, a poor idle and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: The variable-length intake manifold's flaps get gummed up with oil and carbon, and its plastic parts get brittle and break.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Repair kits for the flap linkage can avoid replacing the whole manifold.

issues.t: Harsh shifts or transmission limp mode
issues.sym: Harsh or jerky gear changes, or the car gets stuck in one gear with a warning message.
issues.why: The 7-speed automatic's fluid is called 'lifetime' but breaks down, causing harsh shifts. The conductor plate (the internal circuit board with the speed sensors) can also fail at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned. A fluid and filter service often helps harsh shifts; speed-sensor codes usually point to the conductor plate.

issues.t: Supercharger coupling wears out (AMG 5.5L)
issues.sym: A rattle or chattering noise from the front of the engine at idle and a loss of boost and power.
issues.why: The rubber coupling (isolator) that drives the supercharger breaks down with age.
issues.next: Have a specialist confirm the noise source and replace the coupling before power drops further.

issues.t: Secondary air pump failure
issues.sym: Check engine light with emissions codes, sometimes a failed inspection. The car usually drives normally.
issues.why: The secondary air pump that helps the engine warm up the catalytic converters fails, often from moisture.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the pump and valves checked before an emissions test.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve covers and rear main seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell, or oil on the engine and transmission.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets and the rear crankshaft seal harden and leak at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have the leak pinpointed. Valve cover gaskets are a moderate job; the rear main seal needs the transmission removed.

issues.t: Fuse/relay module (SAM) fails from water
issues.sym: Random electrical faults: lights, windows, wipers or locks acting up, and false warning messages.
issues.why: The signal acquisition modules (SAMs) that control many functions corrode when water gets in, often from blocked drains.
issues.next: Check for wet carpets and clear any blocked drains. A specialist can test and replace or repair the affected module.

issues.t: Front control arm bushings and ball joints wear
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, vague or wandering steering and uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings and ball joints in the front suspension wear out over time on every generation.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and get an alignment after any parts are replaced.

issues.t: Wrong software coding can affect fuel shutoff (recall)
issues.sym: The fuel gauge may read wrong, the check engine light may come on, or the speedometer may be off after a workshop visit.
issues.why: Some cars got an incorrect software coding during service. Besides gauge problems, the fuel pump might not shut off after a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 08V-303. The dealer will recode the software free.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The timing chain, its tensioner and the camshaft adjusters wear, especially when oil changes have been stretched out. Left alone, the chain can jump teeth and damage the engine.
issues.next: Don't ignore a cold-start rattle. Have a specialist check timing codes and the tensioner; it is far easier to fix early.

issues.t: Turbocharger oil feed lines leak
issues.sym: Oil residue around the turbochargers, a burning-oil smell or light smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The fittings on the oil lines that feed the turbochargers start leaking with heat and age.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed; oil dripping on the hot turbos is a fire risk, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Sudden coolant loss from cracked pipe or thermostat housing
issues.sym: A low-coolant warning, a puddle of coolant, a sweet smell or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: Plastic coolant pipes and the thermostat housing crack with heat cycles and can let coolant out quickly.
issues.next: Stop if the engine overheats. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the cracked part replaced.

issues.t: Hood rubber seal can fall onto exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning-rubber smell from the engine bay, or a seal that looks loose at the back of the hood.
issues.why: A rubber seal at the rear of the engine compartment can stick to the hood, pull loose and land on hot exhaust parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 15V-088 and 15V-505. The dealer will add retaining clips or replace the seal free.

issues.t: Side sections of LED tail lights may not light (recall)
issues.sym: The outer parts of the LED tail lights stay dark, making the car harder to see from the side at night.
issues.why: A lighting controller software error.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-137. The dealer will update the lighting software free.

issues.t: Hood latch bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In a worst case, the hood could open while driving.
issues.why: On CLS550s built in December 2011, the hood secondary latch striker bolts may not have been tightened enough.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 12V-533. The dealer will check and retighten the bolts free.

issues.t: Airbag control software may be incorrect (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. Airbags might not deploy correctly in a crash.
issues.why: Some control units on certain 2012 and 2014 CLS550s were programmed with the wrong software.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 17V-177. The dealer will update the control unit software free.

issues.t: Emergency call system may report wrong time or location (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in daily driving. After a crash, the emergency call could send an inaccurate location.
issues.why: A software fault lets the emergency call system's date and time drift, which can throw off the location it sends.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-787. The fix is a free over-the-air or dealer software update.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake won't release or apply
issues.sym: A parking brake warning light or message, or the parking brake doesn't release or set properly.
issues.why: The motor in the electronic parking brake actuator can seize over time.
issues.next: Don't drive with the parking brake dragging. Have the system scanned and the actuator replaced.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate rattle (AMG 5.5L)
issues.sym: A metallic rattle from the turbos, mostly at low speed or when coasting.
issues.why: Heat wears the wastegate linkages on the twin-turbo AMG V8.
issues.next: Have a specialist confirm the source. Worn wastegate parts can sometimes be repaired without replacing the turbo.

issues.t: 48-volt mild-hybrid system faults
issues.sym: EQ Boost or 48-volt warnings, reduced boost assist, a no-start, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The 48-volt battery and the integrated starter-generator can develop faults, and Mercedes issued a bulletin for 48-volt battery software on 2019–2021 cars that could keep the check engine light from warning of a real fault.
issues.next: Get warnings checked promptly. Ask the dealer about 48-volt battery software updates and warranty coverage.

issues.t: Coolant pump wire can chafe on fan (recall)
issues.sym: Engine temperature warning, overheating, or the 48-volt system shutting off.
issues.why: The power wire for the electric coolant pump can rub against the engine fan and wear through.
issues.next: Stop if the engine overheats. Check your VIN for recall 19V-605; the dealer will inspect and reroute or repair the wire free.

issues.t: Engine can stall from powertrain controller reset (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off unexpectedly while driving.
issues.why: Software in the central powertrain controller can reset itself while the car is moving.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for recall 18V-761. The dealer will update the controller software free.

issues.t: Steering rack locknut can break (recall)
issues.sym: Steering may feel stuck or hard to turn in one position.
issues.why: A locknut inside the steering rack can break under high load.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-850. The dealer will replace the steering rack free.

issues.t: Transmission wiring can corrode and short (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly transmission warnings, or smoke or a burning smell in rare cases.
issues.why: On AMG CLS53 models, the transmission wiring harness may be routed so its connector corrodes and short-circuits, which can start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 22V-533 and 24V-445. Even cars fixed under the first recall need the newer harness replacement.

issues.t: 48-volt ground connection can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; possible burning smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The 48-volt ground cable connection in the engine bay may not have been tightened properly and can overheat.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-100. The dealer will inspect and repair the connection free.

issues.t: Fuel pump can shut down and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: The engine loses power or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The fuel pump may fail and shut down.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-445. The dealer will replace the fuel pump free.

issues.t: Trunk 12-volt battery may not be secured (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving. In a crash, the emergency call, power seats, hazard lights and automatic unlocking could stop working.
issues.why: The 12-volt battery in the trunk may not have been fastened down properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-733. The dealer will secure the battery free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image doesn't show (recall)
issues.sym: The center screen goes black or restarts, and the backup camera image doesn't appear.
issues.why: Errors in the MBUX multimedia and camera software.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look back when reversing. Check your VIN for recalls 21V-354 and 22V-232; the fix is a free software update.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, misfires or falling fuel economy at higher mileage.
issues.why: The engine injects fuel directly into the cylinders, so the intake valves never get washed with fuel and carbon builds up on them.
issues.next: Have misfire codes checked; a walnut-blast cleaning removes the carbon.

issues.t: Buckled seat belts may read as unbuckled (recall)
issues.sym: Seat belt warning even though you're buckled in.
issues.why: The front seat belt buckle sensor can report a buckled belt as unbuckled, which turns off the PRE-SAFE and belt pretensioner features.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-788. The dealer will inspect and replace the buckles free if needed.
